name: Feedback renderer
purpose: Deterministic templates for issue title and body, the +1 comment body, and the outbox bundle file. The output is what preview shows and what leaves on submit.
responsibilities: Render the issue title as "[<effective-slug>] <title>" for blueprints and "[rcf-lite] <title>" for core
Render the body with the Evidence and Environment tables, the visible fingerprint line and its HTML-comment twin
Render the outbox bundle header and one section per entry (title first, then body) so a paste is one-shot
Consume redacted strings and the redaction ledger; never re-run redaction itself
internalStructure: src/feedback/render.js exposes renderIssue(entry, redacted), renderComment(entry, redacted, deltaOnly), renderBundle(destinationInfo, entries). All output is UTF-8, LF line endings, ASCII hyphens only (register rule and fingerprint stability).

interfaces.name: renderIssue
interfaces.description: Return { title, body, labels[] } for a create call.

interfaces.name: renderComment
interfaces.description: Return the comment body for a +1 add.

interfaces.name: renderBundle
interfaces.description: Return the markdown bundle string for outbox files.

dependencies.name: TAC-4103-feedback-redact
dependencies.description: The renderer consumes redacted strings the caller supplies.

tradeoffs: Static templates keep the shape reviewable by eye and byte-comparable in tests; the cost is that template drift requires golden updates, which is exactly the discipline the tests exist for.
notes: The docs-site "submit a blueprint idea" form reuses these templates verbatim so triage sees one shape from both producers.
